title: One Saturday and Thirty Years
subtitle: 竞争与比赛 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞争与比赛（文学艺术与体育·竞赛与体育精神）
meta: 主题语境：竞争与比赛（文学艺术与体育·竞赛与体育精神）　|　核心词汇：competition　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 competition 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my sister ① entered a competition she had no chance of winning, and she said the entering was the whole of the summer. The ② competition, meaning the contest and not the prize, took one Saturday and stayed that size; competition, she said, is the only thing in a summer that is judged by how many turn up.

Every ③ competition in that school had the same table, and the ④ competition at the end, meaning the one she kept for the final and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered twice. Competition, my mother said, is nine parts turning up and one part somebody willing to lose; my sister said the turning up is the part that fills the table.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the competition was the whole of the street, meaning the other shops and not the contest. The ⑥ competition, meaning the other shops and not any of that, is the only thing in a street that everybody watches and nobody names; competition, he said, is either something you enter or the only word that means both a contest and the other shops. She said the other shops are the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ competition had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the table. The ⑧ competition of the whole thing, my sister wrote in October, was one Saturday and thirty years of turning up; competition, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to lose well. He said the losing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ competition I remember is the one at the end, which was held in 1973 and is still described as the fullest in the county. A ⑩ competition, my mother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being entered; every competition, she said, is a turning up that has agreed to look like a contest. She said the turning up was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 比赛（指那场比赛本身，与那些奖品相对）
C. 固定搭配：enter a competition 参加比赛
D. n. 比赛（指那个学校里每一届）
E. n. 比赛（指末尾那一届）
F. n. 竞争（指同行、其他店铺）
G. n. 比赛（指账本里提到的那一届）
H. n. 竞争（抽象总称，竞争这一状态）

items.q: entered a competition she had no chance of winning
The competition, meaning the contest and not the prize
the competition was the whole of the street
The competition, meaning the other shops
the competition had become a line in a ledger
The competition of the whole thing
A competition, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: enter a competition 意为“参加比赛”，1959 年姐姐参加了一场她毫无胜算的比赛。
competition 意为“比赛”，指那场比赛本身而不是那些奖品，它占了一个星期六，规模一直没变。
competition 指那个学校里每一届比赛，每一届都用同一张桌子。
competition 指末尾那一届（她留给决赛的那一届），是唯一有人记住过两次的。
competition 意为“竞争”，父亲说竞争就是那条街的全部，指的是其他店铺而不是那场比赛。
competition 为另一个义项，指那些同行店铺而不是那场比赛，是街上人人留意、却无人点名的东西。
competition 意为“比赛”，指账本里提到的那一届，到 1967 年这场比赛成了账本里的一行。
competition 意为“竞争”，姐姐十月写道，整件事的竞争是一个星期六三十年的到场。
competition 意为“比赛”，我记得的是末尾那一届，1973 年举办，至今仍被说成全县参赛人数最多的。
competition 为抽象总称，母亲说一场比赛是唯一会因为被参加而变好的东西。
